thread:
eli: FYI customer reported getting charged for tokens after reconnect + toolcall truncation. looks like provisional tokens never reconciled when the client closed early.

maya: ugh. repro steps? steps + sample ids please. :eyes:

eli: steps I got from support: 1) start streaming 2) reconnect (resume) 3) server emits toolcall mid-stream 4) client sends EOF/close before toolcall completes 5) console shows provisional tokens then a final charge that still includes the truncated suffix. session id s-73f.

lucy: sharing logs (redacted):
```
INFO resume_token=rt-42 session=s-73f route=eu-west toolcall_id=t-901 event=resume
INFO toolcall start t-901 prompt_tokens=84
WARN client_eof session=s-73f time=2026-02-08T14:22:11Z
INFO ledger provisional_add session=s-73f tokens=120 tag=resume-provisional
INFO ledger confirm session=s-73f tokens=260 tag=finalize
```

sanford: the weird bit is the finalize includes both prefix+toolcall+suffix even though suffix was truncated. where is suffix mark-down happening?

eli: our current flow: provisional ledger entries on stream chunks and toolcall start; on finalization we reconcile by session ack window. but if client closes mid-toolcall we rely on toolcall completion hook to subtract provisional tokens. seems that path never fired here.

kevin: possible race between `toolcall_timeout` cleanup and `session_close` path. cleanup might bail and leave provisional counts.

maya: can we query telemetry for missing `toolcall_complete` events for t-901?

lucy: did that, there are NO toolcall_complete events for t-901. we have `cleanup_timer` fired instead.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary release 2026-02-08T13:30 -> rolled to 30% at 13:45 (contains session gc changes).

sanford: aha, canary touched session gc ordering. probable regression.

eli: short-term mitigation: console should show a "provisional" column separate from "confirmed" so ops can tell at-a-glance. long-term fix: ensure `cleanup_timer` triggers a reconciler that reduces provisional tokens and writes a negative ledger entry.

kevin: agree. implementation nuance: negative ledger entries need idempotency and reason tags so billing can be audited. propose event: `provisional_reclaim(session, reason, tokens, causal_id)`

maya: UI ask: flag sessions where provisional > 0 and last_event > Xs ago. add a tooltip: "provisional tokens pending reconciliation".

lucy: question on attribution: do we attribute reclaimed tokens to model fallback route or original route? customers will ask. we should keep original route tag in the negative entry.

eli: yes keep original route & toolcall_id so we can explain. also emit a `reclaim_marker` in traces so Console can link to traces span.

sanford: quick hotfix idea: in the canary rollback we can also add a reconciler lambda that runs every minute to scan sessions closed in last 5m and reconcile any provisional > 0. low risk, quick.

kevin: implementation sketch:
```
for session in closed_sessions(since=5m):
  if session.provisional > 0 and not session.toolcall_complete:
    ledger.append_negative(session.id, session.provisional, reason=\"toolcall-truncate-reclaim\")
    telemetry.emit(\"provisional_reclaim\", {session_id: session.id, tokens: session.provisional})
```
lucy: tests to add: simulate reconnect+toolcall+client-eof, ensure ledger ends at prefix+toolcall-confirmed (no suffix) and console shows a reclaim event.

maya: UX: let's also add an audit link from billing row -> trace span and to the reclaim entry. customers want to see why they weren't charged.

eli: agreed. can we ship the lambda + telemetry + console quickflag as a single patch to rollback branch? ops-bot shows canary currently at 30% so rollback path should be quick.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollback requested by @eli at 14:30 -> rollback started.

sanford: i'll owner the lambda patch, can we pair on telemetry schema? kevin can own ledger negative entry format.

kevin: i'll draft ledger entry format: `{ id, session_id, tokens_delta: -N, reason, original_route, toolcall_id, causal_event_id }` and sample audit message.

lucy: I'll add the console spike: provisional column + reclaim link + tooltip. low-fi screenshot in next message.

eli: thanks team. follow-ups: (1) quick reclaim lambda in rollback (sanford) (2) ledger negative schema + idempotency (kevin) (3) console provisional column + trace link (lucy) (4) add e2e test harness for truncated toolcall case (maya).

maya: tagging @billing for visibility: billing-team please expect a couple negative-entries to show up during rollback reconciler run.

eli: also file a postmortem after rollback and reconciler run. we need a playbook for provisional token leakage. :memo:

kevin: one more thought — longer-term we should make `toolcall_complete` a hard dependency for finalization: if missing, finalization enters "deferred finalize" state until reconciler runs. prevents double-confirmation.

sanford: good note. ok starting on the lambda now, ping when console mock ready.

lucy: mock up uploaded: https://redwood.internal/console-mocks/provisional-flag-v1

eli: perfect. closing thread, will follow up in the postmortem. :thumbsup:
